title: Sell Mineral Rights in Elberta, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Elberta, AL | Baldwin County
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Elberta, AL? Get a hedged, activity-based cash offer for southern Baldwin County farmland near Foley and the Florida line.
heroLead: Elberta's farming roots, planted by German immigrant families more than a century ago, still shape land ownership in southern Baldwin County, right down to how mineral rights were handled when the original homesteads were divided among descendants.
intro: Produce and truck farming built Elberta's early economy, and land here has often stayed within the same families for multiple generations, divided among children and grandchildren over time. Mineral rights on that land followed whatever the original settlement or later estate documents specified, which isn't always something the current generation has reviewed closely.
We buy those interests directly, and the process for a multi-generation Elberta family usually starts with tracing the original homestead deed forward to the present.

sections.heading: Elberta's farming-family land pattern
paragraphs: Because so much of Elberta's land has passed down within families rather than through open-market sales, mineral ownership here is more likely to be an undivided interest split among several relatives than a cleanly surveyed individual share. Sorting that out is often the real first step toward a sale.

sections.heading: Southern Baldwin County's mineral trend
paragraphs: Elberta sits in southern Baldwin County, within range of the broader Smackover-Norphlet trend that runs through the coastal counties, though direct drilling this far south and east has historically been thin. We build value from regional lease and permit comparables rather than local production history.

sections.heading: Confirming a multi-generation family interest
paragraphs: We check Baldwin County's probate and deed records in Bay Minette to trace how an Elberta-area mineral interest has been divided across generations, then confirm the specific share a current family member holds before making an offer.

faqs.question: Our family's Elberta land has been divided among many relatives over the years. Can you still buy our share?
faqs.answer: Yes. We regularly work with individual shares of a larger undivided family interest and help confirm each owner's specific percentage through county records.

faqs.question: Is there any oil and gas activity around Elberta?
faqs.answer: Direct drilling in this part of southern Baldwin County has historically been thin, so we price interests against the broader regional trend rather than local production.

faqs.question: What if we're not sure how our great-grandparents' original homestead was divided?
faqs.answer: We can trace that division through Baldwin County probate and deed records to help clarify what your branch of the family currently owns.

faqs.question: Does farmland still in active use affect the mineral sale?
faqs.answer: No. Active farming on the surface doesn't affect the mineral estate below it, and a sale doesn't interfere with ongoing farm use.
